messages:
tara: Quick question for pricing + eng: should we launch Reserved Throughput as per-route reservations or a pooled org-level reservation? Customer asks are mixed.
noah: Sales notes: two enterprise pilots. One (Globex) prefers per-route for strict SLAs. Other (NovaHealth) wants a single pool across routes to keep UI simpler.
linh: Engineering: pooled is simpler on billing/alloc, but routing needs token accounting either way. Per-route requires per-route tokens & more routing state.
ben: Ops: pooling reduces fragmentation risk, easier to autoscale. But per-route helps customers map spend to product features.
molly: From product POV, packaging options: Tier A (Pooled): 1000rps org pool, flexible routing, $4k/mo. Tier B (Per-route): 100rps per route unit, $60/mo per unit. Add-on: burst credits (100k tokens) $200/mo. Thoughts?
pricing-bot: preliminary sim: fragmentation penalty (expected wasted reserved capacity) = 12% for per-route small customers, 3% for pooled. Revenue delta over a year ~ 8%.
tara: We need launch gating criteria before committing to either default. Proposing: 1) shipping both models (pooled + per-route) is high effort. Maybe ship pooled-first with per-route later.
noah: Sales preference: default pooled, but expose per-route in an "advanced" toggle for enterprise. That lets us land value early.
linh: Dev effort estimate: pooled-only = 4 dev-weeks (routing & billing mapping), pooled + per-route = 10 dev-weeks (extra routing state + console UX).
ben: Can we mitigate customer mapping needs by offering per-route metering in analytics even if billing is pooled? That would be low-effort and might reduce objections.
molly: Agreed - telemetry-only per-route visibility could be a launch must-have. Add to gating: console shows per-route reserved consumption metrics.
noah: Pricing ask from Globex: they'd pay $80/100rps per route if per-route existed. If we default pooled, they may ask for discounts.
ara (typo, but we should keep consistent names)
linh: (ignoring stray)
legal-bot: Suggested contract clause draft: "Reserved capacity is billed monthly; pooling implies shared org-level capacity and the provider may reallocate degraded capacity during emergencies. Early termination fees apply per contract."
tara: Launch gating checklist proposal: a) pooled reservation billing & SKU in catalog, b) per-route telemetry in Console, c) billing flow + invoice preview, d) pilot signed (one pooled customer), e) runbook for fallback if reserved pool > 90% util.
pricing-bot: simulation for recommended default price: pooled 1000rps = $3,500/mo (intro 3mo discount 10%). Profitability target met at 65% utilization.
molly: UX notes: Console needs "Reserve Capacity" flow with slider, region selector, duration (1/3/12 months). Add a confirmation modal that surfaces impact on latency and capacity.
linh: Technical fallback: on pool exhaustion, we enqueue up to 200ms then drop to best-effort with `reserved_downgrade` event. Also emit `reserved_eviction_rate`.
ben: Operations: add alerts: pool_util > 85% for 10m -> paging, >95% auto-throttle policy. Also tag reservations with org-id & contact.
noah: Commercial action: I'll pitch pooled default with per-route telemetry to both pilot customers Monday. See if Globex accepts temporary mapping for billing.
tara: Decision for today: default to pooled-first launch, require per-route telemetry & invoice preview. Per-route billing to be scoped for Q3.
molly: OK. I'll update the Pricing spec doc and add sample SKUs.
linh: I'll open a GH RFC for the routing changes and include the fallback plan.
ben: Ops will add dashboards and paging rules to runbook.
legal-bot: I'll follow up with contract language options and early-termination formula.
tara: Action items: Noah -> pilot commitments; Linh -> RFC + canary plan; Molly -> pricing spec + invoice preview UX; Ben -> dashboards & alerts; Legal -> clause + termination calc. Target: pilot-ready in 4 weeks.
noah: Ack. :thumbsup
